aiExplanation: This function sums up every integer `k` (from `1` to `n`) that evenly divides the array length and for which `nums` is **"sortable"** when split into consecutive chunks of size `k`. For each candidate `k`, it slices the array into equal `partitions`, then checks two conditions chunk by chunk: every element must be **at least as large as the maximum of all previous chunks** (`lastMax`), so the chunks are already in the right order relative to each other, and each chunk must be a **rotated sorted array**, meaning there is at most one position where an element is greater than its circular neighbor `partitions[i][(j + 1) % len]`. If a chunk violates either rule, `cuts` is bumped past `1`, `isSortable` is set to `false`, and the chunk loop stops; otherwise `lastMax` is updated and the next chunk is checked. Any `k` that survives all chunks is added to `res`. Note that this version mistakenly computes the running `max` using `nums[j]` (the global index) instead of `partitions[i][j]`, so `lastMax` is wrong for every chunk after the first, which is why it fails.

notes: Fixed my mistake and simplified code using named continues. Not gonna lie, pretty proud of myself for this one.
aiExplanation: This function adds up every integer `k` between `1` and `n` that divides the array length evenly and for which `nums` becomes sorted when split into consecutive chunks of size `k`. For each such `k` it builds the `partitions`, then walks through them while tracking `lastMax`, the largest value seen in all previous chunks. Inside a chunk, two rules must hold: every element must be **greater than or equal to `lastMax`**, so the chunks are already ordered relative to each other, and the chunk must be a **rotated sorted array**, meaning at most one element is bigger than its circular neighbor `partitions[i][(j + 1) % len]` (tracked by `seenCut`). The moment either rule breaks, the labeled `continue next_k` jumps straight to the next candidate `k`, skipping the remaining chunks entirely. If all chunks pass, `k` is added to `res`, and the final total is returned.
